name: listpush
algorithm: Per round grow a list of u64 from empty by n single pushes of splitmix64 values and one extend by a slice of n/4, read every element back, free it; the wrapping sum of the elements plus the length (README.md).

skip.c: no std growable array in C (a realloc loop written by hand would be a stand-in)
skip.mk-wrap: the checksum already uses the wrapping operators; growing a list has no arithmetic to wrap

no_counts: B24 does not apply: an idiomatic row compares libraries, each with its own growth policy; the checksum (every element and the final length) checks every result
notes: Allocators named (B20's rule, applied to allocators): mk HeapList over sys.heap.Alloc(), std's general heap; rust Vec over System (HeapAlloc); zig std.ArrayList over std.heap.smp_allocator; go append over the garbage-collected runtime allocator (GOGC=100, labelled); cs List<ulong> (Add, AddRange) over the Workstation GC heap (labelled).
